issue: On plain-error review of a Rule 11(b)(3) challenge to a guilty plea's factual basis, what must a defendant show to establish that the error affected substantial rights: a reasonable probability that, but for the error, he would not have pleaded guilty, or only that the record as a whole fails to provide a sufficient factual basis for the plea?

sides.position: The defendant must show a reasonable probability that, but for the error, he would not have entered the plea (Dominguez Benitez standard).
cases: United States v. Bryant, 976 F.3d 165 (2d Cir. 2020)
United States v. Castro-Trevino, 464 F.3d 536 (5th Cir. 2006)
United States v. Monzon, 429 F.3d 1268 (9th Cir. 2005)
United States v. Schuster, No. 24-2942 (3d Cir. 2026)

sides.position: The defendant need only show that the record as a whole fails to provide a sufficient factual basis to support the guilty plea.
cases: United States v. Carillo, 860 F.3d 1293 (10th Cir. 2017)

quote: There is some disagreement among our sister circuits as to what is required to satisfy this standard in the context of a Rule 11(b)(3) challenge to the sufficiency of a guilty plea's factual basis.
cite: United States v. Nicole Schuster, No. 24-2942 (3rd Cir. 2026)
